Prunely Support

Answers to common questions. Still stuck? Email SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD and a human will reply, usually within 2 business days.

When you email us, please include your iPhone model, iOS version (Prunely shows its version in Settings) and what happened. Never send passwords or payment details. We can't see your photos or your Apple ID.

Photo access

Why does Prunely need access to my photos?

To show your photos as cards, measure their size, find duplicates, similar and blurry shots, and, only when you confirm, delete them or add them to albums. Everything runs on your iPhone; nothing is uploaded. "Full Access" lets Prunely see your whole library; read the privacy policy for details.

I tapped "Don't Allow". How do I turn access on?

Open Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > Prunely and choose Full Access (or Limited Access and pick photos). Prunely also has an "Open Settings" button on its no-access screen.

What does Limited Access mean?

With Limited Access, Prunely only sees the photos you picked. Decks, counts and smart groups cover just those items. To add more, use "Choose more photos" in the app, or switch to Full Access in Settings.

Deleting and storage

I deleted photos but my iPhone storage didn't change. Why?

When you confirm a delete, iOS moves the items to the Photos app's Recently Deleted album, not straight to the bin. They stay there for up to 30 days so you can recover mistakes, and they still use storage during that time. iOS frees the space automatically when each item's 30 days are up.

To free the space now:

  1. Open the Photos app (or tap "Open Photos" in Prunely).
  2. Go to Collections > Utilities > Recently Deleted (on older iOS: Albums > Recently Deleted) and unlock with Face ID if asked.
  3. Tap Select, then Delete All.

Deleting from Recently Deleted is permanent. Prunely's Insights screen shows how much is waiting in Recently Deleted versus truly freed; tap "I emptied it" after you empty it to update the totals. iPhone Storage in Settings can take a few minutes to recalculate.

I deleted something by mistake. Can I get it back?

Yes, within 30 days. Before you confirm, everything you swipe to delete waits in Prunely's Review tray, where you can restore any item. After you confirm, open Photos > Recently Deleted, select the item and tap Recover. Prunely notices recovered items and returns them to your decks.

I use iCloud Photos. What happens when I delete?

With iCloud Photos on, your library is the same on all your devices, so deleting a photo on your iPhone also deletes it from iCloud, your other devices and any Shared Library (after the 30-day Recently Deleted period). Prunely reminds you before you confirm.

If "Optimize iPhone Storage" is on, some originals are only in iCloud. Opening them makes iOS download them from your iCloud, which can take a moment and uses data; a progress ring shows on the card. You can turn off these downloads in Prunely Settings (cards then use the smaller preview). Prunely shows whether each item is on your iPhone or in iCloud, and its Insights split freed space into "on this iPhone" and "iCloud", because deleting iCloud-only items frees iCloud storage rather than iPhone storage.

What is the free delete allowance?

Swiping, sorting and finding duplicates are free. Free users can also delete up to the free allowance shown in the app (1 GB or 500 items in total, whichever comes first). Items beyond that stay safely in your tray until you upgrade, and you can delete as many as fit in what's left for free. Pro removes the limit and the ads.

How does Prunely find duplicates, similar and blurry photos?

It uses Apple's on-device Vision framework to compare photos and measure sharpness. Nothing is sent anywhere. The first scan of a large library can take a while and continues where it left off; you can pause it any time. Favorites and photos you've already kept are protected and never pre-selected for deletion.

Purchases and subscriptions

How do I restore my purchase?
  1. Make sure you are signed in to the App Store with the same Apple ID you used to buy Prunely Pro (Settings > [your name] > Media & Purchases).
  2. Open Prunely, go to Settings and tap Restore Purchases (it is also on the Pro screen).
  3. If you got Pro through Family Sharing, make sure Purchase Sharing is on for your family group.

Restoring needs an internet connection to reach the App Store. If it says nothing was found, email us with the approximate purchase date (never send card details); we can't see your Apple ID, but we can help you check.

How do I cancel my free trial or subscription?

Subscriptions are managed by Apple. Deleting the app does not cancel a subscription.

  1. Open the iPhone Settings app.
  2. Tap your name, then Subscriptions.
  3. Tap Prunely Pro, then Cancel Subscription (or Cancel Free Trial).

Or, inside Prunely: Settings > Manage subscription opens the same Apple screen.

To avoid being charged after a free trial, cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends. The app can send you a reminder 2 days before the trial ends if notifications are on. If you cancel during a trial, Apple may end Pro access right away. If you cancel a paid subscription, you keep Pro until the end of the period you paid for. Apple's guide: Cancel a subscription from Apple.

How do I get a refund?

Apple processes every payment, so refunds come from Apple: go to reportaproblem.apple.com, sign in, choose "Request a refund" and pick the Prunely purchase. We can't issue refunds directly, but email us if something went wrong and we'll do what we can.

I have a subscription. Can I switch to Lifetime?

Yes. Buy Lifetime in the app, then cancel the subscription in Settings > [your name] > Subscriptions so it doesn't renew. The app reminds you to do this. Apple decides whether any unused subscription time is refunded.

Why do I see ads, and how do I turn them off?

The free version is funded by ads. Prunely Pro (subscription or lifetime) removes all ads. To stop personalized ads without buying anything, choose "Ask App Not to Track" (or change it later in Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking) and review your choices in Prunely Settings > Ad Privacy Choices. Details are in the privacy policy.

Your data

How do I delete my Prunely data?

Prunely has no account and keeps no data on any server, so there is nothing for us to delete on our side.

  • To start over: Prunely Settings > Review everything again (clears decisions not yet committed; your photos are untouched).
  • To remove everything: delete the Prunely app (touch and hold its icon > Remove App > Delete App). This removes all its data from your iPhone. It does not delete any photos and does not cancel a subscription.

A two-number free-allowance counter stays in the iPhone Keychain so the free allowance can't be reset by reinstalling; it contains no personal information. Data collected by ad partners is covered in the privacy policy.

Does Prunely upload my photos or need the internet?

No uploads, ever. Prunely works offline. It goes online only for App Store purchases, ads in the free version, iCloud Photos downloads (optional) and Apple Maps place names (off by default). Check it yourself in Settings > Privacy & Security > App Privacy Report.
